hoverDefinition: A DCF values a defined future cash stream by discounting it at a matched rate. In an FCFF model, discount explicit forecasts and the end-of-forecast terminal amount to obtain operating value before the claims bridge.

covered: Forecast date conventions, matched FCFF/WACC, separate terminal amount, no double-counting and conditional operating value.
deferred: Full forecasting, terminal reinvestment estimation, changing-rate models, professional calibration and complete claims valuation are deferred.

objectives.statement: Discount explicit FCFF and an end-of-horizon terminal value without repeating cash.
objectives.evidence: Place the terminal amount at its supplied date and distinguish operating from equity value.

context.timeframe: Independent fictional teaching scenarios. Worked examples and practice start separately; they are not consecutive company-case rounds.
assumptions: All FCFF inputs are complete before debt service and match the hypothetical effective annual WACC.
Cash occurs at year ends. Supplied terminal value is at the final forecast year end and covers only later cash flows.
No additional initial investment, excess cash, debt or other claim is folded into the operating value unless explicitly stated.
Retain precision and round displayed INR lakh at the end. Terminal values are assumptions, not sale guarantees.

framework.limitations: Conceptual teaching assumptions, with INR lakh as a unit rather than a jurisdiction. No tax rate, financing term, reporting classification, valuation input or management buffer is a current rule or market recommendation. Applicable framework, jurisdiction, reporting period and effective amendments require separate study.

mechanism.title: Define the asset and forecast perimeter
paragraphs: For these FCFF examples, estimate operating value from future cash after operating taxes/reinvestment and before debt service. Discount at a matched WACC. A valuation of equity cash after debt service requires a different rate and perimeter.
The valuation date is time zero. A cash flow already included in a forecast must not also be added separately as a balance-sheet asset or a second investment item without reconciling the perimeter.

mechanism.title: Place the terminal amount at its own date
paragraphs: Operating value = sum of explicit FCFF_t/(1+WACC)^t + terminal value_n/(1+WACC)^n. The supplied terminal value covers cash after Year n. Year n FCFF remains an explicit period cash flow; including it once does not duplicate the terminal stream.

Terminal value is not automatically today’s value. Discount it for the full n periods. The later terminal-growth lesson explains how to estimate it and why WACC must exceed perpetual growth in that model.

mechanism.title: Report a conditional value and the right claims
paragraphs: Separate explicit-period PV from terminal PV so the dependence on long-run assumptions is visible. Compare feasible forecasts and sensitivity rather than presenting an output with many decimals as certainty.

The result here is operating enterprise value. Bridge separately for excess cash, debt and other claims before stating ordinary equity value. The calculation itself does not post a gain, generate cash or establish a market transaction price.

distinctions.name: Explicit forecast and terminal stream
distinctions.explanation: The explicit years and the later stream cover different dates.
distinctions.whenItMatters: Avoid adding the first terminal-period cash flow twice.

distinctions.name: End-of-horizon and current value
distinctions.explanation: Terminal value belongs at the supplied future date.
distinctions.whenItMatters: Discount it with the correct exponent.

distinctions.name: Operating value and equity value
distinctions.explanation: Non-operating assets and non-equity claims need a separate bridge.
distinctions.whenItMatters: Do not label a before-debt result as ordinary equity value.

workedExample.setup: Hypothetical annual FCFF is 12 at Year 1 end, 15 at Year 2 end and 18 at Year 3 end. A supplied terminal value of 180 at Year 3 end covers all cash after Year 3 and excludes Year 3 FCFF. Matched effective annual WACC is 10%. No claims bridge is included.
steps: Operating value = 172.066115..., displayed 172.07. It is not yet ordinary equity value.
workedExample.interpretation: Most value comes from the terminal assumption; that dependence should be visible rather than concealed in one total.

statementEffects.explanation: Effects under the stated simplified scenario. Forecasts and economic values do not themselves create accounting entries.

misconceptions.claim: Add terminal value without discounting it.
misconceptions.correction: Bring the supplied future amount to today.
misconceptions.diagnostic: At which date is terminal value measured?

misconceptions.claim: An FCFF operating value is automatically ordinary equity value.
misconceptions.correction: Reconcile non-operating assets and claims separately.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Who else has a claim on operating value?

misconceptions.claim: Count the explicit final year again inside a terminal amount that starts afterward.
misconceptions.correction: Follow the supplied coverage dates and count each cash flow once.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Which years does the terminal amount cover?

practice.setup: Independent FCFF forecast: 10 at Year 1 end and 11 at Year 2 end. Supplied terminal value 121 is at Year 2 end and covers only Years 3 onward. Matched annual WACC 10%. No non-operating assets or claims bridge is included.
practice.question: What operating value follows, rounded to two decimals?

options.feedback: This adds terminal value 121 as if it were already at time zero.
This discounts the terminal amount for only one of its two years.

hints.text: Place both Year 2 amounts at the same date before discounting.

reflection.prompt: Why is Year 2 FCFF included alongside terminal value?
rubric: Use exponent 2 for the terminal amount.

practice.setup: Independent FCFF forecast: 6 at Year 1 end and 8 at Year 2 end; a supplied terminal value 60 at Year 2 end covers only later cash. Matched annual WACC is 20%. Debt and excess cash have not been supplied.
practice.question: Which value and label are supported?

options.text: Operating value 70.56; ordinary equity value still needs a bridge
options.feedback: This adds the future terminal amount without its full discount.

options.text: Operating value 52.22; ordinary equity value still needs a claims bridge
options.feedback: Value = 6/1.2 + (8+60)/1.2² = 52.222222..., displayed 52.22. It is an operating value; debt, excess cash and other claims require a separate bridge.

options.text: Ordinary equity value 52.22 with no further information
options.feedback: An operating value does not establish all remaining claims.

practice.solution: Value = 6/1.2 + (8+60)/1.2² = 52.222222..., displayed 52.22. It is an operating value; debt, excess cash and other claims require a separate bridge.

hints.text: Identify the common Year 2 date and the valuation perimeter.
Value = 6/1.2 + (8+60)/1.2² = 52.222222..., displayed 52.22. It is an operating value; debt, excess cash and other claims require a separate bridge.

reflection.prompt: What information is still missing for ordinary equity holders?
rubric: Keep operating and equity labels distinct.
